content:
maya: heads up — since ~23:50 UTC we're seeing token-serving tail latency spike (p99 -> 2.5x) for the shared-gpu-apac pool. Affects a handful of small tenants, requests that hit long-context models.
infrabot: 🔔 Alert: high_token_latency detected on cluster apac1 - group=shared-gpu-apac, severity=warning
kevin: any node-level repro? NICs saturated? kernel drops?
maya: early signal looks correlated with big batching jobs from one customer. p50 steady but p99 worse. not full OOMs, just long stalls during kv-cache writes.
liam: could be KV cache thrash if routing is bouncing requests across different variants. do we have affinity enabled for these tenants?
zoe: checking node counters, posting sampled outputs
zoe: ```
# on node gpu-apac1-12
nvidia-smi dmon -s u
GPU  sm   mem   enc   dec
0    23    17    0     0
# ethtool -S eno2
rx_packets: 12452345
tx_packets: 12451234
rx_dropped: 12
tx_dropped: 0
rx_mcast: 0
```
kevin: rx_dropped=12 is small but I want ifq/tx ring saturation or driver drops. also check pod-level perf counters (cgroups).
ana: typo — ana here. quick grep of router logs shows repeated 503s around 23:58 for route /v1/generate -> pool shared-gpu-apac. sample:
ana: ```
2026-06-15T23:58:12Z router[rt-7]: 503 upstream-reset tenant=t-42 route=/v1/generate pool=shared-gpu-apac
2026-06-15T23:58:12Z router[rt-7]: 200 upstream-ok tenant=t-17 route=/v1/generate pool=shared-gpu-apac
```
liam: that pattern screams contention + fallback attempts. If a chunk of traffic is hitting a hot model with big context we may be losing KV locality when requests land on different nodes. affinity or sticky routing would help.
maya: we have affinity=best_effort for shared pool. not strict.
kevin: short-term mitigation: drain the most loaded node and enable strict affinity for the affected tenant(s). cost: possible increased tail elsewhere. willing to do if it buys breathing room.
kevin: runbook snippet to override routing for tenant t-42 (quick hack):
kevin: ```bash
curl -XPOST "https://infra-api.internal/v1/routing/override" \
  -d '{"tenant":"t-42","pool":"reserved-apac-small","ttl_s":900}' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'
```
zoe: we can also add a temporary QoS tag to demote best-effort batchers: `qos=batch-low` on their job definition — reduces batch size and KV churn.
ana: @kevin please check NIC errors on node gpu-apac1-12 and post `dmesg` if any driver resets.
kevin: running `kubectl cordon gpu-apac1-12 && kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` in 10m. will follow with status.
maya: thanks. also let's capture a 30m trace and dump KV hit/miss ratio for the pool. can someone add that to the observability dashboard?
liam: i'll add a temporary chart (kv_cache.hit_rate by pool) and set an alert if p99 < 0.6.
infrabot: Note: scheduled maintenance window at 02:00 UTC for apac1 — keep in mind routing fallback will run if we shift nodes.
ana: cost note — moving t-42 into reserved-apac-small will add ~0.08 GPU-hrs per minute (ballpark). ops ok with that?
maya: budget ok for emergency. prefer to keep it temporary until we root cause.
zoe: follow-up action items: (1) kevin drain node, (2) liam add kv metric/dash, (3) ana run tenant routing override if needed, (4) maya collect request traces and sample prompts.
kevin: cordon/drain done. currently migrating pods off gpu-apac1-12. no kernel errors in dmesg; only a tx timeout from 23:57 that cleared.
maya: after drain tail p99 dropped back to ~1.1x baseline. looks promising. will keep monitoring for 30m.
liam: filing a short postmortem/ops note: need to evaluate making affinity stricter for long-context models and add per-pool KV miss alerting.
maya: tagging @platform-owners for a follow-up on policy change. thanks all :thumbsup:
